item.title: Can Tinubu’s education reforms rescue a generation? – Inside Alausa’s ambitious agenda
item.description: By Joseph Erunke, Abuja With nearly 46 million children reportedly captured in a new education data system, almost 250,000 Nigerians undergoing technical skills training and the government claiming to have returned one million out-of-school children to classrooms, the Tinubu administration is making an ambitious case for an education turnaround. But can impressive figures translate into lasting educational transformation? For decades, Nigeria’s education crisis has been defined by millions of children outside classrooms, overcrowded schools, inadequate facilities, poorly equipped laboratories, frustrated teachers and graduates struggling to find employment despite their qualifications Now, in the office of the Minister of Education, Dr Tunji Alausa, a digital dashboard is offering a different picture–one the minister says provides an unprecedented opportunity to monitor schools, track enrolment, identify infrastructure gaps and examine the distribution of teachers and pupils nationwide. With a few clicks, Alausa explained, officials can drill down into individual schools to examine enrollment figures, the number of girls, available facilities and teaching personnel. For a country long challenged by fragmented education statistics, this represents a potentially significant shift. But the real test of Nigeria’s education reforms is not how impressive the dashboard appears in Abuja. It is whether the technology delivers better classrooms, competent teachers, improved learning outcomes and greater opportunities for millions of children. That is the central question confronting Alausa as he presents President Bola Tinubu’s education reforms as the beginning of a measurable turnaround. Alausa Speaking while receiving notification of his selection for Vanguard’s Public Sector Icon of the Year award, the minister outlined six priority areas: technical and vocational education and training, science and technology education, reducing the out-of-school population, girls’ education, data and digitalisation, and improving educational quality and teacher effectiveness. Together, these priorities seek to address a fundamental contradiction in Nigerian education: expanding access without guaranteeing learning, producing graduates without adequate practical skills and increasing enrolment without providing sufficient infrastructure. With Nigeria’s population estimated at approximately 220 million and a youthful demographic, Alausa argued that education reform was imperative. The challenge is to turn this demographic advantage into economic productivity rather than allow it to deepen unemployment, inequality and insecurity Perhaps the most consequential element of Alausa’s presentation was the ministry’s cloud-based education dashboard, which he said captures information on nearly 46 million children. item.title: To save Esan language from extinction, I’ll do anything – Dr. Mabel Imooje
item.description: By Fred Iwenjora Dr. Mabel Imooje holds a doctorate degree in linguistics from Bayero University, Kano. The staff of National Institute for Hospitality and Tourism, Kano is making name as an advocate for the survival of Esan Language seen by many researches as one of the indigenous languages set to go extinct if drastic measures are not taken. Imooje travels across Nigeria at her spare time meeting Esan speaking people, giving them reasons to strive to sustain the language. The associate member of Nigerian Institute of Translators and Interpreters. (NITI) tells FRED IWENJORA the inspiration behind this arduous advocacy. She also discusses the hurdles as well as triumphs so far. “My inspiration comes from my passion for Esan language. The language is so very hard wired in my brain that no one needs ask where I come from whenever I speak. Any Nigerian or Edo state native does not need to ask of my tribe before he/she with affirmation will say, ‘you are an Esan’. “My accent is so strong in my speech, and I feel it’s impact should be used in improving language instruction, develop teaching materials and create learning resources for our dear language. Have you documented these in a book? Not yet but it is in the pipeline. I have been fascinated by languages and always wished to speak about theories and workings of indigenous languages. What course of study prepared you for this? I first started with an NCE in English/Social Studies. Later, I got a degree and a master’s in English before switching to linguistics at doctorate level. I did this to really understand how indigenous languages work and of course with special interest in Esan language. I will also say here that I love my language and wanted it documented from my own point of view. On why she went local rather than beginning from abroad with French, Spanish, Italian or even Mandarin, she hinted that “Going local is to encourage indigenous languages to pop up amongst the foreign languages that you just mentioned. No one watches his or her inheritance erode through wreckless abandonments. I decided to go local to save my language from extinction. Esan is both a people and a language spoken in five local government areas in the Edo Central Senatorial district. It is one of the endangered languages of the world. It should be noted that several factors cause language endangerment. These include diminishing number of the native speakers, age, failure to use the language by the children, negative attitude of the native speaker towards the language, rural – urban shift and so on, just to mention but a few. Therefore, my going local is to lend my voice to other crusaders to say ‘no’ to extinction of indigenous languages. You mean we shouldn’t chase foreign languages? I did not mean that. Proficiency in English and any other foreign languages is good for socio-economic mobility and national integration but it can also lead to marginalisation of indigenous languages. item.title: 46-yr-old businessman commits suicide, leaves video message for family
item.description: By Dayo Johnson, Akure A 46-year-old businessman, Akinbolusere Kayode, has reportedly died by suicide in Ondo Town, Ondo State. Sources said he took his life in his office near BOVAS Petrol Station in Igba Town at about 3 p.m. on Thursday. Two empty bottles suspected to have contained poisonous substance were recovered by police detectives attached to the Bolorunduro Division who visited the scene. According to sources, the deceased recorded a video in which he spoke about his business challenges, humble beginnings, and relationship with his wife, whom he praised for standing by him throughout his struggles. He also repeatedly stated that no one pressured him into deciding to transfer his properties to his wife and three children. The state Police Public Relations Officer, DSP Jimoh Abayomi, confirmed the incident. Abayomi said the two empty bottles suspected to have contained Sniper insecticide were recovered from a nearby bush during the police investigation. He added that preliminary findings indicated that the deceased recorded a video before his death in which he lamented the hardships he faced in life. The video has since circulated widely on social media. His remains were evacuated and deposited at the State Hospital morgue for preservation and further examination. Police said no signs of foul play or visible injuries were observed on the body during the initial examination. The Commissioner of Police in the state, Felix Ohagwu, has ordered a thorough investigation into the circumstances surrounding the incident to determine the actual cause of death. Ohagwu urged members of the public to refrain from speculation and allow investigators to carry out their work. He also advised individuals experiencing emotional distress, marital difficulties, or other personal challenges to seek timely support and assistance rather than resorting to actions that could endanger their lives. item.title: 2027: Obi not a threat in Lagos; we’ve corrected 2023 mistakes — APC
item.description: Chieftains of the All Progressives Congress, APC, in Lagos State said on Thursday that the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Mr. Peter Obi, is not a threat in the state, as the mistake of 2023, when Obi won the presidential election in the state, has been corrected. The APC stalwarts stated this while fielding questions from journalists at the launch of the political movement established by the daughter of President Bola Tinubu and Iyaloja General of Nigeria, Dr. Mujidat Folasade Tinubu-Ojo, in Abuja. The movement, named the Iyaloja General Movement (IGM), is to mobilise votes for President Tinubu’s re-election in the January 16, 2027 presidential election. The Lagos State Director-General of the movement, Barrister Adejumbo Omofumilewa, said the inauguration served as a mini-rally in support of Tinubu ahead of the 2027 elections. Omofumilewa expressed confidence that the APC would perform better in Lagos State in the next presidential election, saying the party had addressed the factors that led to its loss in the state during the 2023 presidential poll. He attributed the outcome of the previous election to the party’s failure to adequately assess the political situation in Lagos, describing the experience as a betrayal. “What happened in 2023 that made our candidate lose the presidential election in Lagos State has already been taken care of, because now, everybody is following him,” he said. Omofumilewa also dismissed the prospect of opposition parties posing a serious challenge to the APC in Lagos, insisting that the ruling party had a strong presence across the state. “Obi is not a threat, neither is any party a threat in Lagos State. We are in charge,” he said, adding that the party was politically and organisationally positioned to secure victory in 2027. On his part, the Director-General of IGM, Dr. Nasiru Ladan, said the movement had already attracted over 2,500 support groups, with more organisations expressing interest. Ladan said the groups had been integrated into the movement’s structure and that the organisation was building a database of supporters across states and local government areas. “We have just started; it has been launched today, and we have machinery in motion in all the states, local governments, up to the ward level,” he said. He explained that the movement’s grassroots strategy was designed to translate its organisational structure into votes for the APC in 2027. According to him, the movement plans to deploy 10 facilitators to each polling unit, with each facilitator expected to mobilise 100 voters. He said the initiative was expected to help the movement achieve its target of 10 million votes, although he did not provide a breakdown of how the target would be measured or independently verified. item.title: 2027: How we will curb election violence — INEC
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi The Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, has unveiled an intelligence-led security framework to curb violence ahead of the 2027 General Election, vowing to hunt down anyone who threatens its ad-hoc staff, National Youth Service Corps NYSC members or permanent personnel. INEC Chairman, Prof. Joash Amupitan SAN, disclosed this in Gombe on Tuesday while declaring open the North-East Zonal Interactive Meeting with Staff and Readiness Assessment for the 2027 General Election. The Commission in its daily bulletin said it was shifting from reactive, election-day deployments to a framework designed to protect voters, personnel and electoral materials before any ballot paper is moved. INEC said its collaboration with the Nigeria Police Force, the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps NSCDC, the Department of State Services DSS, the Armed Forces and other paramilitary agencies under the Inter-Agency Consultative Committee on Election Security ICCES has, according to him, been fundamentally restructured. The new framework, which the Commission terms the “ICCES Tentacle,” extends inter-agency security coordination from national and state headquarters directly down to the most remote Local Government Areas and Registration Area Centres. Amupitan told the gathering that no election, however well planned administratively, could be deemed credible if voters, election personnel and observers operate under physical threat or fear of violence. He explained that the framework rests on three pillars, the first being “Map and Mitigate.” Under it, the Commission will use Electoral Risk Management (ERM) tools to identify security flashpoints, seasonal threat factors and local vulnerabilities early, so that security agencies can deploy proactive measures long before ballot papers arrive. The second pillar, “Ensure Safety,” provides a protective umbrella over all electoral personnel, technological assets, including Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) devices and server infrastructure, and, most importantly, the voter. The third pillar, “Guarantee Access,” is aimed at ensuring that each of the 176,846 polling units nationwide remains a safe, peaceful and dignified space for the exercise of democratic rights, regardless of geographical remoteness or historical security challenges. According to him, the collaboration among the agencies had already produced concrete results. He disclosed that joint operations led by the DSS recently uncovered a covert plot by criminal kingpins targeting the Commission’s ad-hoc staff and Youth Corps members. Amupitan said swift, intelligence-led intervention neutralised the threat, and the principal orchestrators were arrested and are currently undergoing prosecution. “Let me send a clear message from Gombe,” Amupitan said, warning that anyone who attempts to threaten, intimidate or harm ad-hoc staff, NYSC members or permanent personnel of the Commission would be hunted down and brought to justice under the

item.title: Niger Illegal Miners: Detainees drank urine, sweat in NSCDC cell before 33 died – Report
item.description: Details have emerged of how alleged illegal miners held in a cell at the Niger State Command of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC) drank urine or sweat because they had no access to drinking water before 33 of them died. Read Also: Full List: Names of 37 miners who died in NSCDC custody In a report submitted by the Independent Investigation Committee, constituted by the Federal Ministry of Interior to investigate the deaths, it was discovered that the male cell had no running water and its toilet was not functioning. The report quoted survivors as describing how they experienced extreme heat, dehydration and overcrowding, while they were unable to move freely inside the approximately 12-square-metre cell. The Jonathan Kure-led 10-member committee authenticated 33 deaths occuring inside the male cell between 8 p.m. on 16 September and 7 a.m. the following day 17 September. The committee said the detainees had no drinking water, while officers ignored warnings about overcrowding and the risk of suffocation. According to the copy of the report obtained by PREMIUM TIMES, the deceased persons included 14 minors. The report, which painted a deplorable, harsh condition of the cell, stated that there were 41 survivors. It found that about 50 male detainees, including children, were confined in the cell, which had a solid metal door and inadequate ventilation. “The Committee finds that officers responsible for the cells failed to reduce the overcrowding, ignored prolonged cries and banging of the cell door and wall and did not provide emergency help,” the report said. Under the dehumanising condition of the male cell, the report said, there was “no water” and “toilet not functional”. It added that “detainees drank urine or sweat.” The situation in the female cell was barely better. The report said there was also “no drinking water” there, except from relatives. The toilet was also “non-functional but usable with fetched water,” according to the report. It added that relatives were prevented from bringing food to detainees on Wednesday, 16 September, the committee said. Warnings ignored The committee found that medical personnel had warned officers about the danger posed by the overcrowded cell before the deaths. Mariam Nelson, an NSCDC medical unit personnel, told the committee that she cautioned the cell guards, Usman Ndamaka and Hassan Mohammed, on the evening of 16 September that the overcrowding could cause suffocation. She said she advised them to leave the metal door unlocked to improve ventilation, but they ignored her warning. The report said detainees began experiencing symptoms, including eye irritation, burning throats, difficulty breathing, excessive sweating and intense thirst, from around 7:15 p.m. on 16 September. They subsequently began shouting for help and pleading for water. An armoury guard, Ahmed Abubakar Wushishi, told the committee that he heard persistent banging and screams from the cell between 1 a.m. and 2 a.m.

item.title: Pharmacists warn against patronising street medicine vendors
item.description: •Say adulterated drugs can cause collapse of health sector By James Ogunnaike; Shina Abubakar & Deola Badru Pharmacists have warned Nigerians against patronising street medicine vendors following the growing threat posed by fake and counterfeit medicines in the country. Read Also: Deadly goods on sale: How fake products damage organs, destroy lives Speaking on the prevalence of counterfeit and substandard medicines in the country, they stressed that the problem poses serious risks to public health, including treatment failure, toxic reactions and potential damage to vital organs such as the liver and kidneys. They therefore called for stricter monitoring of medicines imported into the country, improved regulation of drug manufacturing and distribution and greater public awareness of the dangers associated with purchasing medicines from unauthorised sources. According to Pharm. Franklin Uzoezie: “Fake drugs, also known as counterfeit medicines, are products that do not meet the required standards or do not contain what they claim to contain. This could involve the active ingredient, the strength or dosage, or even the packaging. In some cases, a medicine may claim to contain a particular drug but contain none of it. In other instances, it may contain the drug but not in the correct quantity or strength. All these are examples of counterfeit or substandard medicines. The increasing circulation of fake and substandard medicines in Nigeria has become a major public health concern “The truth is that even healthcare professionals may find it difficult to distinguish between fake and genuine medicines just by looking at them. Their appearance, packaging and other features may be almost identical. In some cases, counterfeit products may even look better than the original medicines. Simply examining a medicine with the naked eye may not be enough to determine whether it is genuine or counterfeit. Appropriate laboratory analysis may be required to establish its composition and quality “When a medicine is counterfeit or substandard, it may contain the wrong ingredients, an incorrect quantity of the active ingredient, or potentially harmful substances. This can make the product ineffective or toxic to the body. The most important precaution is to know where you obtain your medicines. We often advise patients and members of the public not to buy medicines from just any place where they are being sold. Nigerians must purchase their medicines from licensed pharmacies and other legally authorised medicine outlets. “As patients and members of the public, we should not choose where to buy medicines solely because a seller offers a lower price or is conveniently located. We must prioritise the safety, quality and authenticity of the medicines we use. Purchasing medicines from approved sources, strengthening regulatory oversight and improving public awareness would help reduce the risk of exposure to counterfeit and substandard products”. item.title: Deadly goods on sale: How fake products damage organs, destroy lives
item.description: *Everyday purchases now turn to health hazards *Patients end up paying twice for treatment —Adefunke Adeniyi *Counterfeit drugs damage kidneys, liver — Amarachukwu Enahoro *Adulterated drugs can cause collapse of health sector — Pharmacists warn By Chioma Obinna It is an understatement to say that Nigeria is currently battling a health crisis. Virtually every product, drug, food or drink is being counterfeited in the country and the consequence is fatal. Toddlers are no longer safe because counterfeit baby foods are everywhere. Parents now need to exercise caution in the choice of biscuits to give to their children as some biscuits have been discovered to contain toxic. A tablet swallowed to cure malaria could end up damaging the kidneys or liver while a bottle of drink bought to quench thirst could expose the consumer to dangerous substances. Similarly, cooking oil packaged under a trusted brand could contain ingredients far removed from what the label promises. For millions of Nigerians, the growing menace of fake and substandard products has turned everyday purchases into a potentially deadly gamble, with consequences ranging from failed treatment and organ damage to disability and death. The scale of the threat is underscored by the National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC), which reported destroying unsafe, falsified and non-compliant regulated products worth ₦22.73 billion between January and August 2026. Yet, beyond the billions of naira in seized and destroyed goods lies a more disturbing reality: the human cost of a trade that preys on consumers, undermines medical treatment, drains family resources and puts lives at risk. Health experts have therefore raised the alarm that harmful substances in counterfeit medicines, drinks and food products can damage vital organs. The question now is no longer just how much Nigeria is losing to fake products, but how many lives are being put in danger. When the medicine fails The danger is particularly serious when counterfeit or substandard medicines are used to treat common illnesses such as malaria. A patient experiencing fever and body aches may buy an antimalarial, take it as directed and expect to recover. But a medicine containing insufficient active ingredients, no effective ingredient or an inappropriate substance may fail to treat the illness, allowing the patient’s condition to worsen. Dr Amarachukwu Enahoro, a medical doctor and public health physician at Lagos University Teaching Hospital (LUTH), said counterfeit medicines could defeat the very purpose for which they were purchased. “The consequence for that person might be that the main purpose for which this medicine was put, which is to treat malaria, will not be achieved,” she said. “The second implication is that it can now cause damage. item.title: Masussuka: Life, preaching, death
item.description: From Abdullahi Izma Yamadi, Ibrahim Musa Giginyu, Katsina & Dalhatu Liman, Abuja The murder of Katsina-based Islamic cleric, Sheikh Yahaya Ibrahim Masussuka, has stirred emotions and sparked conversations around the life and times of a popular preacher seen through different lenses. To his army of followers, he embodied peace, dignity and tolerance for religious differences. To his critics, he was a controversial scholar whose religious ideology and preaching were questionable. Masussuka was shot dead alongside his associate, Adamu Abubakar, on Monday evening in front of his house at Dutsin-Ma, Katsina State, in an attack claimed by the extremist group, Ansaru. Amnesty International has called on the Nigerian government to conduct a thorough investigation into the killing and ensure that those responsible are brought to justice. The 47-year-old cleric subscribed to and preached Quranic teachings, but, to greater extent, disregarded Hadith, the sayings and practices of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) – a stance that placed him at variance with his critics. He alleged that a lot of Hadiths being attributed to the Prophet were not from him, saying they were concocted by some people out of mischief. Masussuka reportedly began preaching at the tender age of 13 and rose to prominence with the advent of social media, through which he established himself as one of the most vocal clerics among the Qur’aniyun Islamic sect. Through his active social media platforms, his preaching gained more recognition, increasingly attracting attention from other sects with different ideologies. Masussuka’s increased visibility drew controversies around his ideology. One major controversy surrounding Masussuka’s teachings and ideology revolved around his rejection of certain Hadith traditions as authorities and forms of religious practice. According to other sects, his doctrine that only the Qur’an serves as the gateway to religious practice goes contrary to a larger belief that both the Qur’an and the Sunnah of the Prophet are central sources of Islamic guidance. Disagreements over his ideology became more pronounced and his teachings were challenged on several occasions. Though disagreement on the interpretation and authority of Hadith has long existed among Muslim scholars, Masussuka’s unique stance on the matter placed him at odds with scholars who considered his teachings inconsistent with established Islamic traditions. Amid growing scrutiny of his preaching, the Katsina State Government, on November 18, 2025, announced that Masussuka would be required to defend his teachings before a committee of Islamic scholars established based on the several calls. The meeting, however, didn’t see the light of day due to undisclosed circumstances, as he continued to challenge other sects that go against his ideologies. item.title: Parallel campaigns within APC
item.description: From Hope Abah (Makurdi), Promise Adagba (Akure) & Abdullahi Abdulrahaman Chakwa (Gusau) & Ibrahim Musa Giginyu, Katsina While the All Progressives Congress (APC) officially kicked off its presidential campaign last week, a major hindrance to its effective spread in all the geopolitical zones and states in the country has remained the lack of synergy in many states. Weekend Trust checks revealed that there are many states where leaders of the party claiming to work for the reelection of its presidential candidate, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, prefer to work in isolated camps, without as much as involving other leaders in its operations. This, our correspondent learnt, is due to unresolved leadership disputes, personality clashes and the bid outdo each other to prove the one with the bigger political worth. The intensity, however, varies in degree from state to state, with some openly defying each other, while some put up a façade of working together, but beneath the surface are trying to undermine each other’s efforts. Investigations reveal that in states where the governors joined the APC only after winning elections, the process of integrating the party structure on ground has not been concluded, leading to suspicion between those who moved the governors and those they met on ground. In states like Plateau, Taraba, Adamawa and Kano, there are still vestiges of animosity between the two major camps of the defecting governors and those they met on ground. In states like Anambra and Osun, where the governors are members of other parties but have been integrated into the APC presidential campaign council, the preexisting party structures there have shown that they are not comfortable with the arrangement. States like Benue, Ondo, Katsina, Zamfara have shown that the contending forces are not aligned to work together for the reelection bid of its presidential candidate due to unrestrained rivalries between the governors and other powerful figures from the party in their states, who have the ears of Abuja. Our correspondents capture what is going on in some of the states. Masari yet to attend Radda’s campaign rallies in Katsina As the Katsina State chapter of the All Progressives Congress (APC) begins its 2027 re-election campaign, the Special Adviser to President Bola Ahmed Tinubu on Political and Other Matters, Alhaji Ibrahim Kabir Masari, is yet to attend any of the party’s major campaign activities in the state. Masari, who is considered one of the influential APC figures in Katsina, was absent during the inauguration of the Dikko/Tinubu Campaign Council by Governor Dikko Umaru Radda. He was also missing at the official flag-off of the campaign in Funtua Local Government Area. However, rather than joining the governor at the public campaign events, Masari is said to have intensified separate political consultations within and outside Katsina State ahead of the 2027 general elections. item.title: Our governments are not serious about solar power — Prof. A. T. Suleiman (former president, Solar Energy Society of Nigeria)
item.description: Prof. Ahmed Tijjani Suleiman, Emeritus Professor of Energy Engineering, was trained at Ahmadu Bello University, Zaria, where he taught for a few years. He moved to many places, including the University of Sokoto, where he rose to become the Deputy Vice Chancellor. He subsequently became the Vice Chancellor, Federal University of Technology, Yola and for a brief period, Acting Vice Chancellor, University of Abuja. He has also served in the public sector in his state, Jigawa, as commissioner, and was two-time president of the Solar Energy Society of Nigeria. Prof. A. T. Suleiman, who died recently, granted this interview on January 28, 2024. Weekend Trust republishes it in his honour. Let me start by asking you about the early days in Ringim, Jigawa State. I was born in 1945; on September 28th. I remained there for the normal six, or seven years before you are circumcised and then sent to Quranic school outside town. So, I can say my earliest years in Ringim lasted between 1945 to 1950-51. The tradition then, most of our parents didn’t like ‘boko’; didn’t like this modern education. They saw it as anti-Islam, and so on and so forth. All my seniors were always taken outside town for Quranic schooling when they reached the age that they could be taken to primary school. So they were taken out to (avoid) going to primary school? To escape going to primary school, and I was no exception. Fortunately for me, I was taken not too far away from home. I was taken to Malama Taura, which was just about 13km or so away. Unfortunately, before all these tricks, I may call them, to get me out of town so that I didn’t go to school, the headmaster had already enrolled me; my name was already on the list of those who should join the primary school in the year 1952-53. The pressure was so much on my dad that they had to send my eldest brother to bring me back to Ringim. Where was the pressure coming from? The pressure was from the authorities. They were threatening that for that year, anybody who refused to get his child into school would be taken to Kano, to face the Emir of Kano and tell him why not. My father was ready to do that. To face the emir? To face anybody, rather than allow me to go to primary school. But my mother had a second thought. She looked at all my seniors who were taken away and hidden somewhere and there was never any threat on my father to be taken somewhere. Then she said I should not be the one that would take him to that level. She begged my dad to allow me; to follow the instructions of the local authorities that I should join primary school. And that’s how I found myself in January 1953 as a pupil in what we used to call Junior Primary School, Ringim. So, after the normal four years of primary school then, there was the Senior Primary School. We are on the eastern side. item.title: 5 years after, attack victims remain displaced
item.description: For more than five years, home has remained a distant memory for many internally displaced persons (IDPs) living in camps in Benue, and Borno, where the hope of returning to their ancestral communities grows increasingly uncertain with each passing day. Weekend Trust highlights the plights of these IDPs. Why we haven’t returned home – Benue IDPs In Benue State, thousands of internally displaced persons have remained in camps for more than five years and unwilling to return to their ancestral homes for fear of being killed as persistent insecurity has continued t, hindering their safe return home. Jacob Ibaah, one of thousands of the Internally Displaced People (IDPs) staying at the Agagbe camp in Gwer West Local Government Area of Benue after it was formally opened in 2021, stayed in different make-shift homes after their displacement from their homes by armed invaders. “The displacement started in my community in 2003. I remember vividly that I was in secondary school when the armed men first came and attacked us. Since then it has been off and on; we tried to go back but we are attacked again. In 2021, the government formally established the Agagbe camp where we are now. “We haven’t returned to our villages because those who tried it were killed. Others barely escaped with life threatening injuries,” Ibaah said. Dooshima Tyohem, another displaced person, and a mother of two at the Abagana camp along Makurdi – Lafia road in Benue State, noted that she had been displaced from her home since 2018. “We can’t go back home because it’s dangerous to do so,” she said. Similarly, Esther Francis, displaced from her Guma village to living in the Abagana camp, lamented that returning home remains a far-fetched dream for most people like her because it still wasn’t safe just as there are no houses to return to. Francis said, “We are eager to return to our ancestral homes but it’s not safe. Men are still being killed as they try to go back to their farms while women are raped. Besides, the promised reconstruction of our destroyed communities by government is yet to be fulfilled.” She said. For Jessica Mbaneneen Halavaan, who has spent eight years at Ugba camp in Logo LGA, the situation in her village remains volatile for any resident to think of returning. “We can’t dare go back home. Any thought of doing so is a suicide mission,” she replied to our correspondent. Anita Tsavwua, a displaced teenager at Anyiin camp in Logo said they fled their homes at Tombu council ward in 2018 after initial attacks which began in 2014. She noted that her village till date remains deserted because the attackers have occupied the area, making it difficult for her parent to return home. EYN IDP camp chairman, John Goma “There is nobody in my village, and we can’t go back because the attackers are still killing people on the road. item.title: Nigeria’s drug battle
item.description: By Itodo Daniel Sule (Abuja), Salim Ibrahim (Kano) & Mumini Abdulkarim (Ilorin) Despite massive seizures, arrest of Nigerians and foreign nationals, prosecution and dismantling of clandestine methamphetamine laboratories linked to international criminal networks by the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA), among others, drug trafficking remains a major challenge in Nigeria. From industrial-scale drug production to cocaine couriers and cross-border syndicates, the persistence of the illicit trade raises questions about the sophistication of criminal networks and the factors sustaining the business. The growing drug problem has continued to impact negatively on the health and general wellbeing of many Nigerians, especially the youth population. Many families and households note that they are going through a lot of trauma and pains in the management and rehabilitation of their children and loved ones who have become victims of drug addiction. According to data from the NDLEA, over the last five years, a total of 96,157 suspects, including 250 drug barons, have been arrested; 15, 833, 856.3kgs of illicit drug seized with 2,099.96 hectares of cannabis farms destroyed. Within the same period, the agency secured 18,691 convictions while 54, 517 were counselled and rehabilitated. Between January 2026 and September 2026 alone, data showed that 18,290 arrests have been made with illicit drug seizures of 698,488.76kgs while 81.69 hectares of cannabis farms have been destroyed across the country. Within the same period, a total of 2,568 convictions were recorded while 5,681 were counselled and rehabilitated. The agency has also recorded the dismantling of four industrial meth laboratories across four states in recent months. Besides the destructions of meth laboratories, international drug traffickers, including those from South Africa and other parts of the world, have also been arrested in recent months, with some already facing prosecution. The agency also announced drug recoveries across several states, including Lagos, Kano, Bauchi, Niger, Edo, Ondo, Taraba, Oyo and Delta, anong others. Notwithstanding the massive seizures, arrests, convictions and destruction of illicit drugs by the agency, the drug trafficking challenge remains potent, with experts saying that Nigeria is not just a transit route for illicit drug but also evolving as a production hub. In this report, Weekend Trust examines some of the factors making Nigeria a drug trafficking destination and production hub, impacts on drug users and abusers, nexus between drug trafficking and insecurity, and the way forward. item.title: The Cross that killed, the Cross that kills
item.description: By Fada Oluoma Sometimes last year i went to purchase a crucifix for my church at the popular St Cecelia’s sacramental shop in Wuse Zone 2. I was accompanied by my catechist and one other parishioner. We had a short argument on what size to buy. I chose a small one, the catechist argued that we should buy a much bigger one that will occupy up to 80 percent of the space reserved for it. I refused and used my veto power to get the small one. Back then, I wasn’t even thinking about the possibility of a crucifix falling from it’s position and unaliving a priest or anyone in the church. I was driven more by modesty or simplicity. I believe in keeping things as simple as possible. The cross i chose, though small is still very visible to anyone from any corner of that church. I didn’t see the need for a bigger one. The chilling death of a priest by a wooden cross that fell on him gives me more reason to justify my choice retroactively. Both cynics and critics have taken a dig at the Catholic faith over a cross killing a priest in church. To them, it is a caricature of our belief in a good and powerful God. To some other Christians, it is a punishment against idolatry, a sin they accuse Catholic Church of because of images. To some Catholics, it is ominous and a sucker punch. Trying to explain away the deep and uncomfortable contradictions and pains this event causes would be simplistic and probably dishonest, perhaps delusional. We must accept and grapple with the scruples without losing our faith in God. However, the most important thing about it are the lessons we must learn. They are as follows: Death can occur anywhere and any time. People have been killed in churches and other sacred places. Prayer is sacred. Yet, if you pray in a church or grotto with mosquitoes, they are gonna bite and cause you malaria if you don’t take precaution and protect yourself. The prayer you are saying won’t protect you from their bite, unless God decides to use your case as miracle. In churches, safety measures cannot be sacrificed for any pious oestentation, aestetics or expression. A giant crucifix hung on any church must be done in such a way that it will never accidentally fall on anyone. If this safety concern cannot be guaranteed by engineering, a small and lighter one that poses no threat to life could be placed instead. It’s most likely that signs of cracks on the wall where that crucifix was hung had begun showing but people didn’t take notice. There is a difference between the cross that killed the priest and the cross on which Jesus Christ died. It wasn’t that cross that killed Jesus Christ. It was on that cross that Jesus died. The difference between the two is too deep and clear to be mistaken. The cross of Jesus Christ still kills, yes. It kills our egos, lusts, selfishness, fear, doubts, carnal appetites, vices. That’s why Jesus said we should carry that cross and follow him. That is the cross that kills, it is different from a cross that can kill us whe

item.title: Organisers reveals how Kane edged Mbappe to Ballon d’Or win
item.description: Harry Kane won the Ballon d’Or by the smallest margin under its current voting system when he edged Kylian Mbappe by 28 points, France Football which runs the awards, revealed on Friday. The magazine published a breakdown of the votes in its Friday edition. Bayern Munich’s Kane, the first Englishman to win the award since Michael Owen in 2001, received 40 first-place votes from the 100 jurors and a total of 1,055 points. France captain Mbappe of Real Madrid was placed first 23 times and finished with 1,027 points. The previous smallest margin was 41 when Rodri, then of Manchester City, edged another Real player Vinicius Junior by 41 points in 2024. Last season, Paris Saint-Germain forward Ousmane Dembele totalled 1,380 points as he finished 321 points ahead of Lamine Yamal of Barcelona. This summer, Yamal won a World Cup with Spain but he finished third in the voting on 881 points, 174 behind Kane. The Ballon d’Or is awarded following a vote by journalists (one per country) representing the top 100 nations in the FIFA rankings for men, and the top 50 for women. item.title: Gunmen attack ADC guber candidate’s convoy in Sokoto, candidate escapes
item.description: By Musa Ubandawaki, Sokoto SOKOTO — The governorship candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) in Sokoto State, Hon. Manir Muhammad Dan’iya, has reportedly escaped unhurt after suspected gunmen opened fire on his convoy near the Sultan Abubakar III International Airport on Friday night. The incident occurred at about 9pm on October 30, 2026, shortly after Dan’iya had escorted former Sokoto State Governor and Senator representing Sokoto South, Aminu Waziri Tambuwal, to the airport. The candidate’s bulletproof sports utility vehicles were reportedly damaged in the shooting. Confirming the incident, the Sokoto State Police Command’s Public Relations Officer, DSP Ahmad Rufae, said the command had received a report of the incident at the airport and would take necessary action. He added that anyone found culpable would be dealt with in accordance with the law. In a statement issued by his media aide, Aminu Abdullahi, Dan’iya alleged that personnel of the Sokoto Marshal and the Sokoto State Community Guard blocked his convoy and prevented it from passing through the airport area. According to the statement, the personnel claimed they were acting on directives from their superiors not to allow ADC members into Sokoto State. It further alleged that attempts by members of Dan’iya’s security team to resolve the confrontation failed before gunshots were fired, damaging the candidate’s bulletproof vehicles. The statement also claimed that two Department of State Services (DSS) operatives attached to the candidate’s security team were detained during the confrontation. Dan’iya described the incident as a threat to his personal safety and a development capable of undermining democratic freedoms, political participation and peaceful coexistence in the state. The ADC candidate also alleged that earlier on Friday, his team had observed unusual deployments of Sokoto Marshal and Community Guard personnel at various entry points into the state, where vehicles bearing ADC inscriptions were allegedly stopped from entering. He said what initially appeared to be routine security operations had raised concerns about a possible attempt to restrict the movement and political activities of opposition members. “If security personnel can block a gubernatorial candidate, fire gunshots during a confrontation, damage his vehicle and detain officers assigned to his protection, then the people of Sokoto deserve urgent answers. “No one should be above the law, and no security outfit should be used to threaten political opponents,” Dan’iya was quoted as saying. The candidate disclosed that he had visited the Commissioner of Police in the state to formally report the incident, present his account of what transpired and seek intervention. He called on the Inspector-General of Police, the Director-General of the DSS and other relevant security authorities to investigate the incident, identify those responsible and determine whether any unlawful orders had been issued. item.title: NDLEA: No payment for drug tests by Interior Ministry recruits
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi The National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) has announced that applicants undergoing recruitment into four agencies under the Ministry of Interior will not be required to pay for the mandatory Drug Integrity Test (DIT). The agencies are the Nigerian Correctional Service, Nigeria Immigration Service, Federal Fire Service and Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps. The NDLEA said arrangements had been concluded for the exercise, adding that the Ministry of Interior had made bulk payment to cover the testing of all new recruits. Consequently, candidates and personnel participating in the exercise were advised not to make any payment to NDLEA officials, testing centres or through any other payment channel. The agency’s spokesman, Femi Babafemi, disclosed this in a statement, explaining that candidates would be required to access the NDLEA Drug Integrity Test portal through a designated link or access point to be provided on their respective institutional portals. He said the arrangement was designed to ensure a seamless and orderly testing process. According to Babafemi, the portal would enable candidates to complete the necessary registration and documentation before proceeding with the test without making additional payments. The statement added that the agency appreciated the cooperation of the Ministry of Interior and remained committed to ensuring a smooth, transparent and efficient implementation of the exercise. item.title: Sowore, police differ over attack in Ekiti
item.description: Omoyele Sowore, presidential candidate of the African Action Congress (AAC), and the Ekiti State Police Command have given conflicting accounts of an incident at a restaurant in Ado-Ekiti, Ekiti State, on Friday. While Sowore insisted that he and members of his team were violently attacked, the police described the incident as an altercation with some individuals, saying the activist sustained a minor injury. The Police Public Relations Officer, Sunday Abutu, said the command received an alert that Sowore was having issues with some individuals at a restaurant in Ado-Ekiti and immediately deployed operatives to the scene. Abutu said the operatives rescued the AAC presidential candidate and took him to the Police Hospital, Ado-Ekiti, where he was receiving treatment. However, Sowore, in a statement published on his social media accounts, rejected the police description of the incident as an “altercation”. “There was no altercation! We were attacked!” he declared. He accused the Ekiti State Police Command and the Department of State Services (DSS) of attempting to suppress evidence relating to the incident. Sowore alleged that security operatives seized CCTV footage from the restaurant where the incident occurred, claiming that the attackers were captured on camera and accusing the agencies of attempting to shield those responsible. He also faulted the state Commissioner of Police, CP Falade Adegoroye Michael, for describing the incident as an altercation, saying the police commissioner had visited the scene and seen the injuries sustained by the victims but subsequently played down their severity. Sowore further alleged that DSS operatives had been trailing and harassing him since his arrival in the state on Thursday. He claimed that the operatives also threatened the manager of a restaurant where he and his team had earlier eaten, warning him against allowing them to use the premises again. He said the attack occurred shortly after he concluded an interview at MIDAS FM 90.5 in Ado-Ekiti on Friday. Sowore also alleged that some of the attackers came from the Ekiti State Government House and received operational support from DSS operatives. Police Response The police, however, denied reports that the activist was kidnapped, following a social media post claiming that he had been seized by armed thugs and his whereabouts were unknown. Abutu said in a statement that the command wished to clarify that Sowore was not kidnapped but was rescued by police operatives after they received information about the incident. “The command wishes to categorically clarify that Mr. Sowore was not kidnapped. Rather, preliminary information indicates that he had an altercation with some individuals at a restaurant in Ado-Ekiti, following which the police were immediately alerted. “Upon receiving the report, police operatives swiftly mobilised to the scene and successfully rescued him. item.title: Hakimi bags hat-trick as Paris Saint-Germain rip Le Havre to pieces
item.description: Achraf Hakimi rose to the occasion scoring a glorious hat-trick on Friday as a heavily rotated Paris Saint-Germain thumped rock-bottom Le Havre 5-1 in Ligue 1. PSG’s nearest Ligue 1 rivals Rennes lost 5-2 at Nice to allow the champions to open a four-point gap atop the table with 20pts after nine games. Lille host Lens later Friday and can close to within two points of PSG should they win, while Monaco can do the same if they win at Paris FC on Sunday. Le Havre gave PSG a game early on as they suddenly surged forward in numbers with the PSG backline scampering in retreat before striker Josh Maja hammered in the opener against the run of play on 18 minutes. Pushing for a second, Le Havre were carved open in a quick-fire move with Belgian winger Mika Godts racing onto a Hakimi through-ball to level on 26min. Two minutes later Hakimi left the defence trailing and his blistering low drive just inside the near post made it 2-1. The European champions were running the Normandy side ragged before Hakimi scored his second with a fierce free-kick that curled low past the ‘keeper Arnaud Bodard to put PSG 3-1 up. On a lightning break the hosts poured everyone forward in a brave but naive effort to get back into the game, only for PSG to burst back, catching the home goalkeeper way off his line with not a single defender in his half. Senny Mayulu ran around the horrified stopper, and his cool long-range finish hit the back of the net with nobody in the box effectively ending the contest, just after the hour. Hakimi’s hat-trick arrived when he threaded a shot through a forest of players on 69 minutes and had hardly finished a triumphant celebration when coach Luis Enrique subbed him off. Luis Enrique left stars Desire Doue, Vitinha and Joao Neves on the bench while Ousmane Dembele and Georgian attacker Khvicha Kvaratskhelia were missing through injury. item.title: Debt Worse Than Leprosy, Destroys Generations, Says Obasanjo
item.description: Former President Olusegun Obasanjo has criticised President Bola Tinubu over his position on borrowing, declaring that debt is worse than leprosy because it destroys generations. He stated this while speaking at a symposium, a public forum focused on leveraging Artificial Intelligence to solve grassroots problems and accelerate national development in Abeokuta, Ogun State. Tinubu had said in April that borrowing should not be viewed negatively, insisting that the government would borrow when necessary, provided it could repay the loans. President Bola Tinubu (Photo: X@aonanuga1956) But Obasanjo disagreed, describing such a position as absolute nonsense. The former president also questioned Nigeria’s economic performance, recalling that when he established his farm 47 years ago, the naira exchanged at ₦1 to $1 and 85 cents. He challenged the country’s leadership to explain the naira’s depreciation to about ₦1,500 to a dollar, questioning what Nigeria had achieved over the decades. Meanwhile, the guest speaker, historian and public policy scholar, Umar Ardo, has warned that artificial intelligence could deepen Africa’s dependence on foreign powers if the continent fails to control its technology and digital infrastructure. Ardo warned that without investments in chip fabrication, data centres, African-owned datasets and continental cooperation, artificial intelligence could become another tool for managing Africa rather than empowering the continent to determine its own future. Amid criticism, President Tinubu on Thursday defended his administration’s plan to take more foreign loans , arguing that Nigeria needs long-term investment in infrastructure to achieve its ambition of becoming a $1 trillion economy by 2030. The President said the proposed loans would be used to build roads, improve electricity supply, upgrade ports and fund other projects that would create jobs, grow businesses and provide opportunities for future generations. In a statement titled “From Reforms to Delivery: Our Infrastructure Investment and Growth Strategy,” Tinubu said the focus should be on what the borrowed money would achieve rather than how much the government was borrowing. “The key question is not how much we borrow, but what we build, the value we create and the future we leave behind,” he said. He listed the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway, Sokoto-Badagry Superhighway, Trans-Sahara Superhighway, electricity grid improvements and upgrades to major commercial ports in Lagos among the projects the government plans to fund. He said the projects, alongside investments in healthcare, education and vocational training, would connect economic regions, reduce the cost of transporting goods, support farming and industries, and attract private investors. The President said the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway alone could reduce transport costs along its route by 15 to 20 per cent and add up to two per cent to Nigeria’s Gross Domestic Product (GDP) through increased trade, tourism

item.title: 2027: Rivers ADC seeks Ikwerre Elders’ support for Atiku, Amaechi
item.description: By Daniel Abia, Port Harcourt The Rivers State chapter of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) has met with leaders of the Ikwerre ethnic nationality to seek support for its presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, and his running mate, Chibuike Rotimi Amaechi, ahead of the 2027 general elections. The party’s leadership, led by its state chairman, Dr. Chukwudi Dimkpa, visited Ogbakor Ikwerre, the apex socio-cultural organisation of the Ikwerre people, to present its candidates and solicit the elders’ support. Dimkpa told the elders and community leaders that the party considered it important to present its candidates to them as respected statesmen and custodians of Ikwerre cultural heritage. He said an Atiku-Amaechi presidency would focus on moving the country forward, adding that the ADC chose the duo because of their experience and readiness to turn around the nation’s fortunes. The state chairman also used the opportunity to formally present the party’s governorship candidate, Dr. Gabriel Pidomson, his running mate, Mr. David Okumgba, as well as its senatorial, House of Representatives and State House of Assembly candidates of Ikwerre extraction, seeking the elders’ prayers and support. “The ADC as a party recognises Ogbakor Ikwerre as a foremost socio-cultural institution representing the identity, heritage and collective interests of the Ikwerre ethnic nationality,” he said. In his address, Pidomson reminded the elders of the significance of Amaechi’s vice-presidential candidacy, describing him as an illustrious son of Ikwerre who is running alongside Atiku on the ADC presidential ticket. He expressed hope that the Atiku-Amaechi ticket would emerge victorious in the 2027 presidential election, with Atiku becoming president and Amaechi vice-president. Pidomson described the prospect of an Ikwerre son occupying the nation’s second-highest political office as significant to the political history and national participation of the ethnic nationality. He also pledged inclusive governance if elected governor of Rivers State. “If I am elected Governor of Rivers State, I promise to be a governor for all Rivers people, irrespective of ethnic background, political affiliation or other differences. “We will build a new Rivers State that will reflect the collective aspirations of its people, with emphasis on inclusive governance, unity, development and the wellbeing of citizens,” he said. item.title: Fani-Kayode Presents Letters Of Credence, Assumes Duties As High Commissioner In South Africa
item.description: A former Minister of Aviation, Femi Fani-Kayode, has formally presented copies of his Letters of Credence to the Deputy Director-General, Public Diplomacy, and Acting Chief of State Protocol, Mr Clayson Monyela, at the South African Department of International Relations and Cooperation (DIRCO). The presentation on Friday marked an important diplomatic milestone, signifying the formal commencement of Fani-Kayode’s diplomatic functions and his assumption of duties as Nigeria’s High Commissioner to South Africa with effect from October 30, 2026. This photo shows Nigeria’s High Commissioner to South Africa, Femi Fani-Kayode (centre), meeting with South African officials on October 30, 2026. Following the presentation, Fani-Kayode also met with the Deputy Director-General of DIRCO in his office, as part of his initial diplomatic engagements with senior South African government officials. The presentation of copies of his Letters of Credence precedes the ceremonial presentation of his Letters of Credence to South Africa’s President Cyril Ramaphosa, which will take place in a few days. This photo shows Nigeria’s High Commissioner to South Africa, Femi Fani-Kayode (left), presenting his Letters of Credence on October 30, 2026. In a statement dated October 28, the Department of International Relations and Cooperation of the Republic of South Africa explained that the Minister of International Relations and Cooperation had approved a policy change in terms of Article 13 (1) of the Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations, 1961, to replace the current practice where a Head of Mission-Designate would have to present the original Letters of Credence to the President before being considered as having taken up their functions in the receiving state. “The Department wishes to confirm that once the Head of Mission-Designate has submitted the copies of the Letters of Credence to the Chief of State Protocol, the said Head of Mission-Designate is considered to have taken up his / her position as Head of Mission,” the statement read in part. “The Department wishes to furthermore confirm that the original Letters of Credence will still be handed over to the President at the next Credentials Ceremony on a date and time to be communicated. item.title: Lagos warns residents of impending extreme heat
item.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni The Lagos State Government has warned residents to prepare for possible extreme heat and associated environmental and public health challenges as climate outlooks indicate rising temperatures across parts of Africa, including Nigeria. The Commissioner for the Environment and Water Resources, Tokunbo Wahab, gave the advisory on Friday, urging residents to take preventive measures to protect their health and wellbeing. Wahab said the strengthening El Niño climate pattern, alongside the seasonal transition into the dry season, could contribute to unusual temperature conditions, increased heat discomfort, dry spells, dust and deteriorating air quality. He noted that although the intensity and local impact would depend on prevailing weather patterns, residents should take the emerging climate risks seriously. According to him, Lagos, as a densely populated and rapidly urbanising coastal city, could face heightened exposure to extreme heat. “The concentration of buildings, roads and other heat-absorbing infrastructure, coupled with limited green spaces and inadequate ventilation in some neighbourhoods, could intensify temperatures in built-up areas,” he said. Wahab warned that prolonged exposure to excessive heat could lead to dehydration, heat exhaustion and heatstroke, with potentially serious consequences. He identified children, older persons, pregnant women, outdoor workers, street traders, construction workers, waste handlers and people with underlying health conditions as particularly vulnerable. The commissioner urged families, employers, schools and community leaders to pay special attention to these groups and ensure that protective measures were put in place. He also cautioned that extreme heat could worsen air-quality challenges during the dry season, when dust and haze increase respiratory irritation. He added that increased reliance on petrol and diesel-powered generators during power interruptions could further worsen local air pollution. Wahab urged residents to avoid open burning of refuse and adopt environmentally responsible practices. He advised residents to drink sufficient water regularly, wear lightweight and breathable clothing, seek shade and well-ventilated spaces, and reduce strenuous outdoor activities during the hottest periods of the day. He also encouraged schools, markets, workplaces and other public facilities to provide adequate ventilation, access to drinking water and shaded areas. The commissioner urged residents to watch out for warning signs of heat-related illnesses, including excessive sweating, dizziness, headache, weakness, nausea and muscle cramps. “Anyone experiencing these symptoms should be moved to a cooler environment, given appropriate cooling assistance and taken for medical attention where necessary. “Sudden collapse or loss of consciousness should be treated as medical emergencies requiring immediate attention. “Residents with respiratory conditions are also advised to limit expo

item.title: FG assures ECOWAS of peaceful 2027 elections
item.description: By Favour Ulebor, Abuja The Federal Government has assured the Economic Community of West African States, ECOWAS, of its commitment to conducting peaceful, credible, transparent and inclusive general elections in 2027. In a statement on Friday, the Minister of Foreign Affairs, Ambassador Bianca Odumegwu-Ojukwu, gave the assurance during a meeting with the ECOWAS Pre-Election Fact-Finding Mission to Nigeria, led by former Vice-President of Sierra Leone, Victor Bockarie Foh, at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Abuja. Odumegwu-Ojukwu said the Federal Government was committed to ensuring that the electoral process complied with the provisions of the Nigerian Constitution and relevant electoral laws. She described the 2027 general elections as a defining moment for Nigeria’s democracy, expressing optimism that the process would strengthen democratic governance in the country and the West African sub-region. The minister said institutional preparedness, transparent voter accreditation, effective management of election results and timely resolution of electoral disputes were important to building public confidence in the electoral system. She also stressed the need for effective coordination among security agencies to protect candidates, electoral officials, observers and voters before, during and after the elections. According to her, security personnel must perform their duties professionally and impartially while respecting the country’s human rights obligations. The minister further highlighted the importance of voter education and effective enforcement of electoral laws, noting that political parties, civil society organisations, traditional institutions and the media had important roles to play in ensuring peaceful elections. She expressed concern over the dangers of misinformation and disinformation, calling for accurate, accessible and timely information on the electoral process. Odumegwu-Ojukwu also identified the need to improve measures that would encourage the participation of persons with disabilities and other vulnerable groups in the elections. Earlier, Foh said the mission was in Nigeria to assess the country’s preparedness for the 2027 general elections through consultations with relevant institutions and stakeholders. He said the mission had engaged the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, political parties, security agencies, civil society organisations and the media. Foh disclosed that its earlier engagements with stakeholders, including the Inter-Party Advisory Council, the Nigerian Civil Society Situation Room and the Nigerian Union of Journalists, had been constructive. He said the mission’s preliminary assessment suggested a favourable environment for the forthcoming elections, adding, however, that consultations were still ongoing. According to him, the mission would submit a report outlining its findings and recommendations at the end of the exercise. The former Sierra Leonean vice-president welcomed the assurance

item.title: Nigeria, Russia Review 1967 Bilateral Air Services Agreement
item.description: Nigeria on Friday met with the Russian Federation on the sidelines of the Third Russia-Africa Summit in Moscow, Russia, as both countries move to strengthen aviation relations and expand cooperation in the air transport sector. The Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, SAN, led Nigeria’s delegation to a high-level bilateral meeting. At the meeting, the Nigerian delegation, led by Keyamo, held discussions with Dmitry Stanislavovich Zverev, who is the State Secretary and Deputy Minister of Transport of the Russian Federation, on the need to modernise the existing framework governing air services between the two countries. A major outcome of the meeting was the resolution by both sides to renegotiate the Bilateral Air Services Agreement (BASA) between Nigeria and Russia, which dates back to 1967, with a view to establishing a new agreement that reflects contemporary developments and emerging opportunities in international aviation. The meeting centred on the need to modernise the existing framework governing air services between the two countries. According to a statement by the aviation ministry, both countries agreed on a six-month timeline to conclude the negotiations and sign the new agreement in Saint Petersburg, Russia, in April 2027. To facilitate the process, the two sides have constituted their respective negotiating teams to commence work immediately and ensure that the agreed timeline is met. “The proposed agreement is expected to provide an updated framework for bilateral air transport relations and create opportunities for enhanced connectivity, closer institutional collaboration and mutually beneficial engagement between the aviation sectors of both countries,” the statement signed by the minister’s Special Adviser on Media and Communications, Tunde Moshood. The Nigerian delegation included the Director-General of the Nigerian Civil Aviation Authority (NCAA), Capt. Chris Najomo; the Registrar of the Nigerian College of Aviation Technology (NCAT), Dr. Danjuma Adamu Ismaila, as well as directors from the Federal Ministry of Aviation and Aerospace Development and the NCAA. “Beyond the review of the existing air services agreement, the meeting also explored other potential areas of cooperation between Nigeria and Russia,” the statement disclosed. It added that both parties expressed their commitment to examining the opportunities in the coming months, with a view to deepening bilateral relations and identifying areas of shared interest in aviation and related sectors.
